questions.question: How many numbers are there from 300 to 650 which are completely divisible by both 5 and 7?
questions.solution:
LCM of 7 and 5 is 35

⇒ 1st number after 300 which is divisible by 35 = 35 × 9 = 315

Last number which is less than 650 = 35 × 18 = 630

⇒ 630 = 315 + (n - 1)35

⇒ n = 10

∴ there are 10 numbers between 300 and 650 which are divisible by 35

questions.question: Raman can do a work in 5 days, Jatin can do the same work in 7 days and Sachin can do the same work in 9 days. If they do the same work together and they are paid Rs. 2860, then what is the share of Raman?
questions.solution:
Raman can do 1/5, Jatin can do 1/7 and Sachin can do 1/9 of the work in 1 dayRatio of their work in 1 day = 1/5 : 1/7 : 1/9

⇒ Ratio is 63 : 45 : 35 And the amount paid to them also will be in the same ratio.

⇒ Raman’s share {(63)/(63 + 45 + 35)} × 2860

∴ Raman’s share is Rs. 1260

questions.question: If the diameter of a sphere is 14 cm, then what is the surface area (in cm²) of the sphere?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of sphere = 14 cm

**Formula used:**

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr²

**Calculation:**

Radius = 14/2 = 7 cm

⇒ Surface area = 4 × π × Radius²

⇒ 4 × 22/7 × 49

**∴ Area is 616 cm²**

questions.question: If the price of pen decreases by 20%, then a man can buy 10 more pens for Rs 100. What is the new price (in Rs.) of each pen?
questions.solution:
Let the price of 1 pen initially be Rs. X

⇒ Number of pens he can buy now = 100/x

 After 20% discount price of 1 pen = x(1 – 20/100) = 0.8x

⇒ Number of pens he can buy now = 100/0.8x

According to problem statement,

⇒ 100/0.8x – 100/x = 10 pens

⇒ (100/x) × 1/4 = 10

⇒ x = 2.5

∴ the new price is 2.5 × 0.8 = Rs. 2

questions.question: After deducting 60% from a certain number and then deducting 15% from the remaining, 1428 is left. What was the initial number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be y

After deducting 60% from certain number

⇒ y(1 – 60/100) = 0.4y

After deducting 15% from remainder

⇒ 0.4y(1 – 15/100) = 1428

⇒ 0.4 × y × 0.85 = 1428

∴ y = 4200

questions.question: A train travels 40% faster than a car. Both start from point A at the same time and reach point B, 140 km away at the same time. On the way the train takes 25 minutes for stopping at the stations. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of car be x

⇒ Speed of train = x(1 + 40/100) = 1.4x

Time taken by car to cover 140 km

⇒ 140/x

Time taken by train to cover 140 km

⇒ 140/1.4x

According to the problem statement

⇒ 140/x – 140/1.4x = 25/60

⇒ x = (140 – 100)/(25/60)

∴ speed of train = 1.4 × x = 134.4 km/hr

questions.question: A certain sum of money triples itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years it will be five times?
questions.solution:
Let rate be r, principle amount be p and the number of years bet

After 5 years,

⇒ Simple Interest = 3p – p = 2p

⇒ 2p = (p × r × 5)/100

⇒ r = 40

After t years,

⇒ Simple Interest = 5p – p = 4p

⇒ 4p = (p × 40 × t)/100

⇒ t = 10

∴ It will take 10 years

questions.question: If x + (1/x) = 2, then what is the value of x⁶⁴ + x¹²¹?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

(a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b²

**Calculation:**

Given that, 

x + 1/x = 2

⇒ (x² + 1)/x = 2

⇒ x² - 2x + 1 = 0

By using the above formula, 

⇒ (x - 1)² = 0

⇒ x = 1

⇒ x64 + x121 = 1⁶⁴ + 1¹²¹ 

**∴ x64 + x121 = 2**

questions.question: If x = 6 + 2√6, then what is the value of sqrt{(x – 1)} + (1)/(sqrt{(x – 1))} ?
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation:**

Let a=sqrt{(x – 1)} + (1)/(sqrt{(x – 1))}

Squaring both sides, we get:

a² = x – 1 + {1/(x – 1)} + 2

Given x = 6 + 2√6 = x - 1 = 5 + 2√6, i.e. the above expression can be written as:

⇒ a² = 5 + 2√6 + {1/(5 + 2√6)} + 2

After rationalizing 2ⁿd term, we get:

⇒ a² = 5 + 2√6 + 5 – 2√6 + 2

⇒ a² = 12

∴ a = 2√3

The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 32 cm and each of the equal sides is 5/6 times of the base. What is the area (in cm²) of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Let the base be b.

⇒ other sides = 5b/6

⇒ perimeter = 32 = b + 5b/6 + 5b/6

⇒ b = 12

And the other side be = 5b/6 = 10 cm

Using heron’s formula

⇒ Let s = perimeter/2 = 16

⇒ Area² = s × (s – 12) × (s – 10) × (s – 10)

⇒ Area² = 16 × 4 × 6 × 6

∴ Area = 48 cm²

questions.question:
In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle, and ∠DCE = 45°. If CD = 10√2cm, then what is the length (in cm) of AC? CB = BD

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94231af847657343fbb78de087186e8711f6090c9e5075e0a93ece7540460687.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠DCE = 45°

CD = 10√2 cm, and CB = BD

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94231af847657343fbb78de087186e8711f6090c9e5075e0a93ece7540460687.png] 

Since OC is tangent to CE and ∠DCE = 45°

⇒ ∠OCB = 90 – 45 = 45o

Since CB = BD = 10√2over2 = 5√2 cm then ∠OBC will be 90o 

In ΔOBC, 

cos45° = CBover OC (∠OCB = 45° )

⇒ OC = radius = 5√2 × √2 = 10 cm

tan45° = CBover OB

OB = 5√2 cm

AB = OB + OC = 10 + 5√2 (Approximating 10 + 5 √2 = 17.5)

In ΔABC,

Using Pythagoras Theorem,

⇒ AC² = BC² + AB² = (5√2)² + (10 + 5√2)²

⇒ AC² = 50 + (17.5)² 

⇒ AC = √(50 + 17.5²) = √ 356

**∴ AC is approximately 18.5 cm**

questions.question: What is the simplified value of sin2Aover{(1+cos2A)}?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

**sin2Aover{(1+cos2A)}**

**Formula used:**

sin2A = 2sinAcosA 

cos2A = 2cos²A – 1 = 1 - 2sin²A

**Calculation:**

sin2Aover{(1+cos2A)}

cos2A = 2cos2A – 1

⇒ 1 + cos2A = 2cos²A

⇒ sin2Aover{(1+cos2A)} = {2sinAcosA}over{2cos²A}

⇒ sinAover cosA = tanA

∴ sin2Aover{(1+cos2A)} = tanA

∴ its simplified form is 1 – cos²(A)

questions.question: What is the simplified value of 1 + tanA tanAover2?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1 + tanA tanAover2

**Formula used:**

tanA = {2tan{Aover2}}over{1-tan²{Aover2}}

cosA = cos²Aover2 - sin²Aover2

1 + tan²Aover2 = sec²Aover2 = 1over cos²{Aover2}

**Calculation:**

1 + tanA tanAover2

⇒ 1 + {2tan{Aover2}}over{1-tan²{Aover2}} tanAover2 

⇒ 1 + {2tan²{Aover2}}over{1-tan²{Aover2}} = {1-tan²{Aover2}+2tan²{Aover2}}over{1-tan²{Aover2}}

⇒ {1+tan²{Aover2}}over{1-tan²{Aover2}} = sec²{Aover2}over[1 - {sin²{Aover2}over cos²{Aover2}}]

⇒ {1}over{cos²{Aover2}[{{cos²{Aover2}-sin²{Aover2}}over {cos²{Aover2}}}]} 

⇒ 1over cosA = secA

∴ 1 + tanA tanAover2 = secA
